new.headline: You are fitter than the plan assumed, but going from 37 to 53 miles in one week is how injuries start. Next week drops to about 39 miles, and every planned distance is the most you should run, not the least.

answers.question: I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?
answers.answer:
Not at this level, and not by adding miles to every run. The fitness is real. Easy runs at 9:50/mi with heart rate 139, four threshold reps at 7:55/mi with no fade and an evenly paced 20-miler all point the right way.

The problem is that heart and lungs adapt faster than calves, tendons and bones. A 43% jump in one week is where overuse injuries start. They rarely show on the day, so feeling fine now doesn't settle the question. Your tight calves on Sunday night are an early sign of that load.

What you can keep up is steady training at the planned distances. Treat each one as the most you run that day. The plan will keep building, so your extra fitness gets used, just in steps your legs can absorb.

new.analysis:
## What happened against the plan
You kept the shape of the week but made every run longer, so 38 planned miles became 53. Friday's rest was the only day that went as planned.

| Day | Planned | Ran |
|---|---|---|
| Mon Sep 7 | rest | 4 mi easy |
| Tue Sep 8 | 6 mi easy | 7 mi |
| Wed Sep 9 | 8 mi, 3 x 1.5 mi at 8:00/mi | 9 mi, 4 x 1.5 mi at 7:55/mi |
| Thu Sep 10 | 5 mi easy | 7 mi |
| Fri Sep 11 | rest | rest |
| Sat Sep 12 | 4 mi easy | 6 mi |
| Sun Sep 13 | 15 mi, heart rate under 150 | 20 mi, average 149, drifting to 153 |
| Total | 38 mi | 53 mi |

The easy days themselves were spot on, at about 98% in zone 2. The extra rep on Wednesday added a mile and a half of hard running to a week that was already growing.

## Sunday cost the most
Sunday turned an easy 15 into a moderate 20, and that costs more than five extra miles. You rated it 7/10 for effort, the same as Wednesday's threshold session. That is why only 54% of the week was in the easy zones.

At 3h 20m it also went past about 3 hours. Beyond that, long runs add little fitness but keep adding recovery time. Future long runs will stay near 3 hours and get more race-specific by adding marathon-pace miles, not by going longer.

## Why next week looks like this
Next week holds at about 39 mi so your body can recover from the 20-miler. That is still more than the 37 mi you ran two weeks ago, so you are holding your fitness, not losing it.

Wednesday's session is at goal marathon pace instead of threshold. Goal pace is the most race-specific work you can do now, and it is gentler on legs that ran 20 mi three days earlier. Keep your two strength sessions as well; you did both last week.

## The road to Nov 1
If next week goes smoothly, Sep 21 – 27 builds to about 44 mi, with an 18 mi long run that includes miles at marathon pace. One more big long run comes in early October, about 4 weeks out from the race. After that, the taper covers the last two to three weeks.
